nodes.label: Development Phases (0-20)
nodes.rationale: Do not skip phases merely to make a demo look complete.

nodes.label: Required Documentation Set
nodes.rationale: Documentation must not become disconnected from implementation.

nodes.label: Platform Strategy
nodes.rationale: macOS and Windows targets; Linux must not be made impossible, and platform-specific code stays isolated.

nodes.label: Proposed Repository Structure
nodes.rationale: Do not use blindly; the final structure is determined by Graphify plus the actual repository state.

nodes.label: Phase 0-20 feature roadmap
nodes.rationale: Each phase is gated on its own testable exit criterion in docs/ROADMAP.md and committed separately, so no phase is skipped to make a demo look complete.

nodes.label: INCDAW project mission
nodes.rationale: Functional parity with FL Studio-class workflows using independent code, architecture, algorithms, assets, branding and UI — FL Studio 2026 is a FUNCTIONAL reference only.

nodes.label: Absolute User Control Rule
nodes.rationale: Claude must not autonomously implement changes. 'continue', 'go ahead', 'do it', 'fix it' do not count as approval unless an exact plan was shown first.

nodes.label: Audio Correctness Requirements
nodes.rationale: Audio correctness is non-negotiable: sample-accurate timing, denormals, NaN/infinity, buffer and sample-rate changes, offline render equivalence.

nodes.label: Decision Log
nodes.rationale: Every major architectural decision recorded with context, options, tradeoffs and status; never silently replaced.

nodes.label: Definition of Done
nodes.rationale: A feature is not done because UI exists or code compiles; behavior, tests, edge cases, performance, docs and graph accuracy are all required.

nodes.label: Dependency Policy
nodes.rationale: No dependency without approval; name, purpose, license, maintenance, platform support, performance, security and alternatives must be presented first.

nodes.label: Required Feature Workflow (Steps A-E)
nodes.rationale: Graph, research, inspect current state, plan, then STOP and wait for explicit approval.

nodes.label: First Task: Discovery and Architecture Planning
nodes.rationale: On a fresh repository do not start coding; perform complete discovery and architecture planning, then stop.
nodes.norm_label: first task: discovery and architecture planning

nodes.label: Graphify Mandate
nodes.rationale: Graphify is a persistent architectural intelligence layer, not a one-time setup tool; it establishes structure before raw file reads so the repo is not blindly grepped.

nodes.label: Scope Control
nodes.rationale: If implementation reveals another problem, stop and report scope expansion instead of auto-fixing unrelated issues.

nodes.label: Testing Strategy
nodes.rationale: Every core subsystem needs automated tests; add a regression test for every serious bug.

nodes.label: Graphify-first architectural protocol
nodes.rationale: Graph the repository, read GRAPH_REPORT.md, query relationships, and only then open the relevant source files — so planning starts from real structure instead of a grep. Never fake Graphify output.

nodes.label: Critical operating rule: no implementation without approval
nodes.rationale: Default state is RESEARCH -> GRAPHIFY -> PLAN -> STOP -> USER APPROVAL -> IMPLEMENT -> VERIFY. Claude may investigate and plan autonomously but may not edit sources, change dependencies or alter architecture until the displayed plan is approved.
nodes.norm_label: critical operating rule: no implementation without approval

nodes.label: Insert Chain Compilation
nodes.rationale: A MixerNode's inserts compile into a chain in front of its strip; the compiler keeps two index maps per mixer node — where signal enters (head of chain) and where it leaves (the strip) — because a send routed into the destination's fader would otherwise bypass its plugins.

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Mixer and Routing
nodes.rationale: Complete 2026-08-14. Exit criterion is the PDC test, which also asserts that the same test FAILS with compensation disabled — the test proves the mechanism, not just the outcome. Insert chains stayed empty because there was nothing to insert until Phases 13 and 15, and sidechain edges compile to nothing until a plugin can receive one.

nodes.label: Phase 6 — Piano Roll
nodes.rationale: Metal-rendered editing surface. Exit criterion: 60 fps sustained with 10,000 notes, every edit undoable, and no direct model mutation outside the command registry.

nodes.label: Phase 7 — Channel and Instrument System
nodes.rationale: One reference built-in instrument exists specifically to prove the instrument API — the API is built before the instruments.

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Pattern System
nodes.rationale: Complete in two parts (8a model/compilation, 8b UI). A step is an ordinary note (D-016), so the Channel Rack and the Piano Roll edit the same objects. Exit criterion: one pattern placed several times plays identically at each placement and editing it updates all placements.

nodes.label: Phase 9 — Playlist / Arrangement
nodes.rationale: Complete in two parts (9a pattern arrangement with a Pattern/Song transport mode D-017 and compile-time track mute/solo D-018; 9b audio clips with gain, normalize and fades applied pre-mixer). Split/stretch/crossfades, clip pan/reverse, streamed-clip normalize, folders, lanes, markers and grouping are deliberately deferred.

nodes.label: Pre-Fader Inserts (D-028)
nodes.rationale: Inserts run pre-fader because a fader move must not change what a compressor hears.

nodes.label: Multi-Output Plugin Nodes Requirement
nodes.rationale: FL's Transmitter splits a signal into transient and sustain streams each routable to its own mixer track; a linear insert chain would not suffice, so the mixer graph must support multi-output plugin nodes.

nodes.label: plugins::AudioUnitInstance / platform::AudioUnitHost
nodes.rationale: Components are enumerated from the system registry — no scan, no plugin code run — and appear beside scanned CLAP plugins; ClassInfo state travels through the same StateIO seam project files already use.

nodes.label: plugins::HostedPlugin interface
nodes.rationale: The interface the SECOND plugin format forced. PluginNode, the instance manager, delay compensation, plugin state files and the shell's editor windows are written against it; CLAP and AU are two implementations and nothing above the interface knows which is which.

nodes.label: plugins::PluginRegistry (catalogue + blacklist)
nodes.rationale: Startup loads the persisted catalogue and touches no plugin binary at all. The cache key is (size, mtime) so an unchanged library never spawns another child; a crashed library is blacklisted WITH its reason until the user clears it; an unknown TSV version is refused, not guessed at.

nodes.label: plugins::scanOutOfProcess
nodes.rationale: fork/exec where an argv never meets a shell; descriptors are parsed from the child's report and a died-of-signal child is classified as 'crashed' — the outcome the mechanism exists for.

nodes.label: incdaw-pluginscan out-of-process scanner
nodes.rationale: Disposable by design (PLUGIN_HOST.md §3): an unknown plugin's entry code must never run in the DAW's own process, so a crashing plugin costs only the child.

nodes.label: incdaw_plugins layer library
nodes.rationale: Sits BESIDE engine at the same layer rank rather than above it, because PluginNode derives engine::Node; the link therefore reads plugins -> engine -> platform.

nodes.label: incdaw-testcrash.clap (hostile test plugin)
nodes.rationale: The plugin host cannot be tested against third-party binaries and must not be tested against nothing: one well-behaved plugin, one hostile one.

nodes.label: Plugin host architecture pipeline
nodes.rationale: Scanner -> Registry -> Instance -> Parameter System -> State System -> UI Bridge -> Audio Processor -> Latency Reporting -> Automation -> Crash/Isolation Strategy, architected early even though complete support arrives later.

nodes.label: Resolved technology decisions D-001..D-010
nodes.rationale: C++20/Apple clang, CMake+Ninja, direct CoreAudio HAL, os_workgroup realtime scheduling, macOS first with Windows behind platform/, AppKit shell + Metal widgets, CLAP -> AU -> VST3 with VST2 excluded because the SDK is not licensable, closed-source with permissive dependencies only (JUCE rejected on licensing), ad-hoc signed .dmg distribution.

nodes.label: Scanner rides inside INCDAW.app
nodes.rationale: The app copies incdaw-pluginscan into Contents/MacOS at build time so out-of-process scanning still works wherever the app is installed.

nodes.label: CLAP header inclusion discipline
nodes.rationale: third_party/clap is a PUBLIC include on incdaw_plugins because the host's own headers carry clap types; that nothing above plugins/ includes a clap header is a design rule enforced by review, not by the build.

nodes.label: Downward-only layer dependency rule
nodes.rationale: Allowed link order is ui -> app -> project -> engine -> platform, with plugins branching beside engine. Enforced statically by tools/check_layering.py, which fails the build so an architectural violation is as loud as a failing assertion (ARCHITECTURE.md §2).

nodes.label: No re-listing of transitive layer archives
nodes.rationale: incdaw_app already pulls project -> engine -> platform; naming them again puts the same archive on the link line twice and ld warns.
nodes.norm_label: no re-listing of transitive layer archives

nodes.label: app::ChannelRackModel
nodes.rationale: Same headless-model shape as the Piano Roll. The rack and the Piano Roll edit the same notes — a step is an ordinary MidiEvent at the channel's stepKey (D-016) — so there is no step data type for the two views to disagree about.

nodes.label: Command Palette
nodes.rationale: Lists the standard action table beside the menu bar it walks, so an action can never be searchable but unreachable, or reachable but unsearchable.

nodes.label: app::CommandRegistry
nodes.rationale: The registry, not the UI, owns shortcut bindings, menu entries and toolbar actions. CommandRegistry::execute() is the single mutation path into the project model; anything mutating the model outside it is a bug.

nodes.label: INCDAW Project Data Model
nodes.rationale: Project owns Song, Timeline, Track, Clip (Audio/Pattern/Automation), Pattern, Channel, Instrument, MixerNode, RoutingConnection, AutomationLane and AudioAsset as distinct types. The constitution forbids collapsing them into one generic object. The engine holds a compiled read-only view and never owns or mutates model objects.

nodes.label: app::PianoRollModel
nodes.rationale: A headless model holding geometry and hit testing, so a pane's arithmetic is tested without a window; the view turns input into commands and a draw list into pixels, with no path to the project model that bypasses CommandRegistry.

nodes.label: app::registerStandardActions
nodes.rationale: Populates the registry's action table from app/ rather than the shell: a list of what the application can do is not a property of the window system, and a list only the shell can build is one no test can check.

nodes.label: Undo Stack
nodes.rationale: A stack of executed commands, moved from exactly one place — the shell's Edit menu (D-037) — which resyncs every pane afterwards so a step taken in one editor cannot leave another holding indices into rows that no longer exist. Per-pane Cmd+Z survives only as the fallback for when a text field's field editor must win.

nodes.label: P1 — Piano Roll Chord Toolkit (detection, stamp, progression nudge)
nodes.rationale: DONE. app::music plus ChordCommands; Option-click stamps, 1-8 pick the shape, V flips voicing, C names the selection, [ / ] nudge diatonically. Equivalent of FL 2026's Chord Panel, Chord Stamp and Chord Progression tool.
nodes.norm_label: p1 — piano roll chord toolkit (detection, stamp, progression nudge)

nodes.label: P2 — Piano Roll Note Tools (strum, arpeggiate, legato, labels)
nodes.rationale: DONE. NoteToolCommands: S strum (Shift for down), P arpeggiate (Shift for up-down), L legato, F2 rename.
nodes.norm_label: p2 — piano roll note tools (strum, arpeggiate, legato, labels)

nodes.label: P8 — Slicer (onset detection, slice-to-keys, timing pattern export)
nodes.rationale: DONE. engine::audio::detectOnsets (energy-leap with refinement, +/-6 ms on the test loop, no false onsets in steady tone); SliceAssetCommand lands a sampler channel with one zone per slice chromatic from C3 plus the pattern replaying the loop's timing through the tempo map, all in one undo. Fruity Slicer 2 equivalent.
nodes.norm_label: p8 — slicer (onset detection, slice-to-keys, timing pattern export)

nodes.label: P9 — Browser Pane (search, favourites, preview, drag into project)
nodes.rationale: DONE. app::Browser (classification, folders-first listings, capped recursive search, favourites, recents, stage-and-rename persistence); INCDAWBrowserView as leftmost pane with Cmd+B; engine::AuditionPlayer previews mixed after the graph with block-counter buffer hand-over, cross-rate repitch and no allocation. Drops land through commands so each is one undo with stable ids.
nodes.norm_label: p9 — browser pane (search, favourites, preview, drag into project)

nodes.label: Command Architecture (every action is a command object)
nodes.rationale: One mechanism yields undo/redo, keyboard shortcuts, menus, macros, MIDI-learn mapping, command search and scripting. FL Studio's 2026 assistant can organise tracks and adjust parameters precisely because FL exposes such a surface; INCDAW gets the same capability for free by building this way from the start and cannot retrofit it cheaply otherwise.
nodes.norm_label: command architecture (every action is a command object)

nodes.label: Stable 64-bit Entity Identity
nodes.rationale: Every persistent entity carries a stable 64-bit id, unique within the project and never reused; references are by id, never by pointer or index. This is what makes undo, serialization and relinking tractable.

nodes.label: D-012 — A pattern stores its notes per channel
nodes.rationale: Pattern::channels holds a vector of PatternChannelContent because that is the shape the workflow actually has; a flat list forces every consumer to re-group by channel.
nodes.norm_label: d-012 — a pattern stores its notes per channel

nodes.label: D-016 — A step is a note, and its pitch belongs to the channel
nodes.rationale: Steps are ordinary MidiEvents written at a per-channel Channel::stepKey, because a second representation is a second source of truth and the rack and the Piano Roll must not be able to disagree about the same material.
nodes.norm_label: d-016 — a step is a note, and its pitch belongs to the channel

nodes.label: D-037 — Undo and redo route through the shell, not through whichever pane has focus
nodes.rationale: The registry is already the single mutation path (ARCHITECTURE §6), so the single place that moves the stack must also resync every pane; per-pane handlers remain only as the fallback when a text field's field editor must win.
nodes.norm_label: d-037 — undo and redo route through the shell, not through whichever pane has focus

nodes.label: Product Decision: No AI Assistant Features
nodes.rationale: FL 2026's Gopher agentic assistant and ML stem separation are out of scope by recorded product decision. Noted explicitly: the command registry is the scriptable surface such an assistant would need, so the capability is not architecturally foreclosed.
nodes.norm_label: product decision: no ai assistant features

nodes.label: engine::AutomationNode
nodes.rationale: Evaluates every lane per block inside the graph and dies with it, so appliers cannot dangle. Binding is a half-open tick window (D-026): clip semantics fall out — nothing before the clip starts, the last written value holds after it ends.

nodes.label: app/AutomationWriteSession
nodes.rationale: Armed fader/pan moves are captured with their transport ticks, thinned to where the envelope actually bends (a straight ramp keeps two points), and landed undoably; writing over an existing lane replaces only the written range.

nodes.label: engine::BuiltinEffect (Node + ParameterSink + StateIO)
nodes.rationale: One catalogue drives the compiler, the automation registry, the mixer menu and slot naming; a builtin slot is constructed exactly where a hosted plugin's factory would run (D-033), so there is no special casing anywhere above it. Every effect passes a bit-exact null test at transparent settings and matches an independent reference implementation.

nodes.label: plugins::ClapInstance
nodes.rationale: Carries CLAP_EXT_PARAMS, STATE, LATENCY and GUI with hostile-input scepticism: half an extension is treated as none, saves are capped at 64 MB, latency is capped at ten seconds, and parameter values reach the plugin only through a preallocated lock-free queue drained into the block's event list — never through a call, which is what the CLAP concurrency contract demands.

nodes.label: ui/macos/InsertParameterPanel
nodes.rationale: Holds row data and a write block, never an engine pointer — sinks die with their graph, so each slider move re-resolves the slot against the LIVE graph. Panels follow live values at 5 Hz so automation, MIDI knobs and undo are visible, and drags are never fought.

nodes.label: Limiter (Lookahead) builtin effect
nodes.rationale: Fixed 2 ms window because a parameter would leave PDC stale between rebuilds; sliding-maximum gain lands attenuation before the transient and the reported latency enters the graph's existing compensation through the hosted plugins' door.

nodes.label: engine::MidiMapNode
nodes.rationale: The hardware counterpart of the AutomationNode: mappings resolve at compile time through the SAME resolveApplier the automation lanes use (factored out, not duplicated), ride the same graph and write the same smoothed setters, so a knob and a lane cannot disagree about a parameter.

nodes.label: project::ParameterRegistry
nodes.rationale: Key -> normalised-value applier mapping; Entry::apply is a variant of StripApplier or SinkApplier, and which alternative it holds tells the compiler what a lane's target resolves to. Plugin keys are scoped per TYPE ('plugin:<uid>:<param-id>') while the lane's targetEntity picks the instance, so two instances of one plugin share entries.

nodes.label: engine::ParameterSink (D-029)
nodes.rationale: A pure interface for parameter targets that are not mixer strips, reached through an optional Node::parameterSink() accessor so the graph compiler can bind automation onto a node it knows only as engine::Node.

nodes.label: plugins::PluginInstanceManager (D-031)
nodes.rationale: Owns live instances keyed by SLOT id; PluginNode borrows. Before this, every rebuild — every added note — created a fresh instance and silently reset the plugin's live state. Disposal happens only in the retain pass the shell runs AFTER the engine swaps graphs, so it cannot race the audio thread; this is also the precondition editor windows needed to outlive rebuilds.

nodes.label: plugins::PluginNode
nodes.rationale: A hosted plugin as a render-graph node: sums its inputs like a strip (an insert processes the mixed signal), then the plugin runs in place. Mono graphs pass through rather than handing the plugin two aliases of one buffer. Inserts run PRE-FADER so a fader move does not change what a compressor hears.

nodes.label: engine::StateIO (D-030)
nodes.rationale: A pure interface for nodes whose state is an opaque blob, with Node::stateIO() following the parameterSink() capability pattern.

nodes.label: Plugin delay compensation (PDC)
nodes.rationale: GraphBuilder inserts delay lines on short paths into any summing node. setDelayCompensationEnabled exists so compensation can be tested against its own absence — the pass is proven to depend on the mechanism.

nodes.label: Touch and latch automation modes
nodes.rationale: Write spans the pass; touch closes a segment per drag (mixer mouse-up reports gesture ends) so existing envelope survives between drags; latch holds the last value to the stop tick. Switching modes lands the pass first.

nodes.label: project/PluginStateFiles
nodes.rationale: Captures blobs into plugins/insert-<slot-id>.state with stage-and-rename and restores them after a compile; capture runs BEFORE ProjectFile::save, restore after compiling a loaded project. Stage-and-rename means a crash mid-write loses only the new version.

nodes.label: Plugin Blacklist
nodes.rationale: A plugin that crashes or hangs the out-of-process scanner is recorded and skipped on later scans; kept user-visible and user-clearable with forced rescan so the mechanism can never silently hide a plugin forever.

nodes.label: Plugin State System
nodes.rationale: Plugin state is an opaque binary blob owned by the plugin, stored per instance inside the versioned project package; INCDAW never interprets it. Defined here because Graphify flagged it as an under-specified isolated node in the constitution.

nodes.label: Plugin Validation Checks
nodes.rationale: Before a plugin is trusted in a user's project it is checked for I/O sanity, NaN/Inf output, audio-thread allocation (detectable in the sandbox), unload/reload behaviour and state round-trip fidelity; failures are recorded in the registry and surfaced rather than silently tolerated.

nodes.label: PluginRegistry
nodes.rationale: Persisted catalogue (identifier, format, path, name, vendor, category, I/O config, cached parameter list) loaded at startup without touching a single plugin binary, so startup time does not scale with the size of the user's plugin collection.

nodes.label: PluginScanner
nodes.rationale: Runs out-of-process, one plugin at a time, with a hard timeout, so a crashing or hanging plugin can never block a scan or startup; results are cached by path/size/mtime/format so rescans only re-examine changed entries.

nodes.label: Project Archiving (.incdaw-archive)
nodes.rationale: A single zip with all referenced media embedded plus a manifest of required plugins and versions, so opening an archive with missing plugins lists exactly what is needed rather than failing opaquely.

nodes.label: AudioAsset (path + content hash)
nodes.rationale: Recording both a path and a content hash is what allows referenced media to be verified and relinked by content when the path has moved; relative paths inside the project directory, absolute path plus hash outside it.

nodes.label: .incdaw Package Directory
nodes.rationale: A directory presented as a single macOS package rather than one opaque file, buying partial save, streaming load, crash resilience (a corrupted pattern loses one pattern, not the session), version-control-friendly diffs and independent recovery. The trade-off — more files on disk and a packaging step for transfer — is accepted for a document users spend months in.

nodes.label: project.json
nodes.rationale: Holds tracks, channels, mixer, routing and markers as UTF-8 JSON so the document stays human-readable, diffable and debuggable; it indexes patterns by id and filename rather than embedding them.

nodes.label: Clip Gain / Pan / Normalize as Clip Properties
nodes.rationale: They are clip properties applied pre-mixer and must round-trip through the project format, not mixer settings.
nodes.norm_label: clip gain / pan / normalize as clip properties

nodes.label: Extensible Per-Note Property Slot
nodes.rationale: Renamable/labelled Piano Roll notes mean MIDI events need an extensible per-note property slot rather than a fixed struct — a change to the core event type, so it must be designed in early.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Transport
nodes.rationale: Exit criterion is sample-accurate click-track events across tempo changes and loop boundaries, which forces block splitting at event boundaries to be real rather than approximate.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Project Model and Format
nodes.rationale: Full data model with stable 64-bit ids, .incdaw v1.0 package, migration framework and first fixture, missing-media relinking. Exit criterion: round-trip and determinism tests both pass and the v1.0 fixture loads.

nodes.label: Phase 5 — MIDI Engine
nodes.rationale: CoreMIDI timestamped I/O, UMP/MIDI-2.0-capable, MPE-ready events and a per-note extensible property slot. Exit criterion: recorded MIDI reproduces input timing within tolerance across a tempo change.

nodes.label: Deterministic Fuzzing of Byte-Level Readers
nodes.rationale: Randomly corrupted and truncated project files must be rejected cleanly — never crash, never silently lose data. Extended to plugin scanning in Phase 13 and, by Phase 19, to every byte-level reader (project package, WAV, SMF).

nodes.label: INCDAW Project Format v1.x
nodes.rationale: INCDAW_PROJECT_VERSION is written from the very first project file INCDAW ever saves, because CLAUDE.md §2 forbids ever creating an unversioned project format.

nodes.label: Prime Directive: Third-Party Plugins Are Hostile Input
nodes.rationale: Plugins crash, hang, allocate on the audio thread, report wrong latency, return NaN, open windows on the wrong thread and misbehave on unload. Every DAW with a reputation for instability earned it here, so the host is never permitted to assume good behaviour.
nodes.norm_label: prime directive: third-party plugins are hostile input

nodes.label: Missing-Plugin Placeholder Retains State
nodes.rationale: A plugin missing at load does not discard its state — the node becomes a placeholder holding the blob so installing the plugin later restores the session intact. A blob the plugin rejects is a named warning, the plugin plays defaults, and the blob stays on disk.

nodes.label: Missing Media Handling and Relinking
nodes.rationale: Designed in from v1.0 rather than added later: assets verified by path then hash, all misses reported in a single dialog, relinking searching project directory → configured paths → content hash → the user, and a project with missing media still opens with placeholder assets preserving every clip position, gain and edit. Nothing is discarded.

nodes.label: Per-Pattern Files (patterns/*.pat)
nodes.rationale: Patterns are JSON in v1.0 rather than binary because the speed concern was never measured and PERFORMANCE.md §4 forbids optimising ahead of measurement. What v1.0 commits to is one file per pattern, so an individual pattern's encoding can change to binary later without touching project.json, without a major bump for the rest of the document, and without invalidating any other file. Deferred, not foreclosed.

nodes.label: ProjectFile::migrate
nodes.rationale: The single place that decides whether a path from a given version exists at all; even purely additive versions declare their path because silently accepting unknown versions is how a loader starts dropping fields. Upgrades needing context the hook lacks (separate pattern documents, frame→tick conversion needing the tempo map) happen at their read sites instead.

nodes.label: Phase 4 Format Test Gate
nodes.rationale: Six gates: round-trip, determinism, version fixtures, missing media, corruption rejected cleanly, and fuzzing of randomly corrupted files — together they define what 'the format works' means.

nodes.label: manifest.json
nodes.rationale: Always plain, minimal JSON and the first thing read, so that any future version can read it whatever else changes. It is also the only place embedded timestamps are allowed, which is what makes byte-identical re-saves possible.

nodes.label: Migration Chain (v1.0 → v1.1 → v2.0)
nodes.rationale: Migrations chain step by step so there is never a direct v1.0 → v3.0 path to maintain; migration is one-way and non-destructive with the original backed into history/ first; a project saved by a newer INCDAW is refused with a clear message rather than opened optimistically.

nodes.label: Permanent Version Fixtures (tests/fixtures)
nodes.rationale: Every released format version gets a permanent frozen fixture that must keep loading forever, and a migration that breaks an old fixture fails CI. They are frozen documents rather than regenerated by the current writer, so they keep testing the past instead of the present.

nodes.label: Format Version History (1.0–1.5)
nodes.rationale: 1.0 first format; 1.1 per-channel pattern channels plus swing and tick-based clips; 1.2 stepKey; 1.3 samplerZones; 1.4 midiMappings; 1.5 instrumentParameters (D-034). Every version after 1.0 is additive, and defaults on read reproduce exactly how the older documents behaved (e.g. stepKey defaults to 60).

nodes.label: Non-Functional Requirements Table
nodes.rationale: Each requirement names both its source clause and the mechanism that verifies it: realtime guard, transport tests, equivalence test, fixture tests, misbehaviour matrix, layering test, review policy, decision-log review. A requirement with no verifier is not accepted.

nodes.label: Increment 4 — Mapping, Zone and Instrument Editors
nodes.rationale: Instrument parameter persistence landed first (D-034, format 1.5): values live in the model and the compiler applies them through the instrument's sink at every build — the mixer's source-of-truth rule, which also makes the edits undoable.
nodes.norm_label: increment 4 — mapping, zone and instrument editors

nodes.label: Golden-File Audio Test
nodes.rationale: A fixed project rendered to WAV and compared against a checked-in reference catches DSP regressions no unit test would notice; references are regenerated only by a deliberate reviewed commit that explains the change.

nodes.label: Realtime Safety Guard Test
nodes.rationale: Debug builds arm a thread-local guard on the audio callback with a global operator new/delete override and instrumented locks; any allocation or lock on the audio thread fails the suite on the commit that introduced it, so the rule is enforced at the moment of violation rather than discovered later.

nodes.label: Render Equivalence Test
nodes.rationale: Offline render must be byte-identical to a realtime capture. If it fails, the architecture is wrong; the test is not relaxed. Written before its Phase 17 gate.

nodes.label: Save Determinism (byte-identical re-save)
nodes.rationale: Stable collection ordering by id, no timestamps outside manifest.json, and no absolute paths where relative works. Determinism is what makes the round-trip regression test meaningful and the format usable with version control.

nodes.label: INCDAW's Own JSON Writer
nodes.rationale: Used instead of a library because the determinism requirement rules out any implementation that iterates object keys in hash order.

nodes.label: Update and Downgrade Policy
nodes.rationale: An older project opens in a newer INCDAW through declared migrations and a newer project is refused by an older build with a clear message rather than opened hopefully; downgrading INCDAW does not downgrade projects, so the old app must be kept to reopen a newer-format project.

nodes.label: Single-Source Version Stamping
nodes.rationale: The version lives in ONE place — CMakeLists.txt project(VERSION …) — and is stamped into build/VERSION, the bundle and the DMG file name at build time, so the artifact can never disagree with the code about what it is. src/app/Version.cpp mirrors it for the status line and must be bumped in the same commit.

nodes.label: engine/audio/AudioEdits (editor verbs)
nodes.rationale: Pure region operations with half-open clamped ranges and no I/O anywhere near the DSP. Destructive edits are undoable by snapshot: undo restores bit-exactly and redo writes the RECORDED result rather than re-applying, because gain would compound.

nodes.label: engine/dsp/Fft (own radix-2)
nodes.rationale: Allocation-free and proven against a naive DFT, so no dependency approval (§41) was needed for spectrum analysis.

nodes.label: project::renderProject / OfflineRender
nodes.rationale: NO separate offline DSP: the same compiler, graph and block loop the audio callback runs, captured instead of played. Assets always preload (never stream) offline because determinism is the contract. Proven float-for-float equal to a captured realtime-style drive.

nodes.label: app/ProjectSession (lifecycle decisions)
nodes.rationale: The headless decisions — recents-list update, autosave destination, autosave-newer comparison — split out of the shell exactly like the view models, so they are testable. Autosave never touches the dirty flag, the title, the recents, or the user's file.

nodes.label: engine::dsp::resample (windowed-sinc)
nodes.rationale: Blackman-Harris, 32 taps/side, correct anti-alias cutoff when downsampling; measured < -60 dB RMS error. Phase 18 replaced two transcendentals per tap with a 512-phase x 64-tap table plus linear phase interpolation: 547.9 ms -> 18.6 ms for 10 s stereo (29x faster) with the quality test unchanged.

nodes.label: engine::dsp::timeStretch (offline WSOLA)
nodes.rationale: Transient locking makes clicks survive both directions exactly once; stereo-coherent alignment; pitch shift via windowed-sinc. Warped clips render at compile time and play through the graph.

nodes.label: INCDAW_REALTIME_GUARD option
nodes.rationale: Asserts on allocation/locking inside the audio thread; armed in Phase 2 and compiled as a PUBLIC definition on incdaw_engine so every consumer of the engine inherits the guard in debug builds.

nodes.label: incdaw_engine layer library
nodes.rationale: Realtime core: knows nothing above it and holds no OS symbols, which is what makes the render graph testable headlessly and portable.

nodes.label: incdaw_platform layer library
nodes.rationale: The ONLY layer permitted to contain OS-specific code; keeps CoreAudio/CoreMIDI/AudioToolbox/AppKit symbols out of every layer above it and makes a Windows port a matter of a second platform implementation.

nodes.label: incdaw_project layer library
nodes.rationale: Data model, serialization and versioning. Deliberately does NOT link incdaw_plugins: hosted plugins reach the graph only through the injected insert factory (D-028).

nodes.label: Export Audio options dialog
nodes.rationale: Fronts everything project::OfflineRender already implemented: master/stems/tracks, WAV or AIFF, 16/24-bit PCM or float32, target rate through the windowed-sinc resampler, tail, normalize, TPDF dither, loop-range export. Later gained background rendering over a project copy with a modal progress window and cancel.

nodes.label: .incdaw versioned project format
nodes.rationale: Versioned from v1.0 with staged writes, a migration hook and a frozen hand-written fixture per version. Every later addition (1.1 pattern channels, 1.2 stepKey, 1.3 sampler zones, 1.4 MIDI mappings, 1.5 instrument parameters, 1.6 markers/regions/stereo width) is ADDITIVE with its migration path declared, so older files load and repeat saves are byte-identical.

nodes.label: Core data model (no collapsed entities)
nodes.rationale: Project, Song, Timeline, Track, Clip, Pattern, Channel, Instrument, Plugin, Mixer Node, Automation, MIDI Event, Audio Asset and Routing Connection stay distinct; collapsing them into one generic model is explicitly forbidden.

nodes.label: Definition of success (three signal chains)
nodes.rationale: MIDI->instrument->channel->mixer->effects->automation->master->render, audio input->recording->clip->playlist->..., and plugin->parameter->automation->mixer->render must all share ONE transport, timing, project state and undo architecture rather than being disconnected tools.

nodes.label: Measure-before-optimise performance strategy
nodes.rationale: Everything optimised carries a documented before/after measurement, and everything left alone carries the measurement that justified leaving it alone.

nodes.label: Project format requirements
nodes.rationale: Versioned, migratable, deterministic, portable, resilient to missing media, and able to store plugin state, automation, MIDI, routing and arrangement. Never create a project format without versioning.

nodes.label: Realtime guard cannot see elided allocations
nodes.rationale: Tests that deliberately allocate must call ::operator new directly rather than use a new-expression, or the optimiser elides the allocation and the test silently passes in Release.
nodes.norm_label: realtime guard cannot see elided allocations

nodes.label: ParameterRegistry (plugin registration)
nodes.rationale: Entries generalised to StripApplier OR SinkApplier over engine::ParameterSink; registerPluginParameters is all a plugin needs to become automatable. Keys are plugin:<uid>:<param-id> and the lane's targetEntity (the insert slot id) picks the instance.

nodes.label: Audio Units (v2 + v3) Support
nodes.rationale: Second in implementation order: native to macOS and therefore mandatory there; Apple SDK headers verified present on the machine.

nodes.label: Plugin Parameter System (D-029)
nodes.rationale: Discovery happens once per plugin TYPE at first instantiation on the main thread and is cached per uid; every parameter maps to INCDAW's generic automation subsystem so there is no plugin-specific automation code anywhere (CLAUDE.md §10).

nodes.label: Shared-Memory Audio Ring Buffer (host boundary)
nodes.rationale: Audio crosses the host/plugin boundary as memory, not function calls, so the same code path works in-process and out-of-process.

nodes.label: VST3 Format Support
nodes.rationale: Third: widest plugin availability, and Steinberg's withdrawal of GPLv3/proprietary dual licensing in favour of MIT (SDK 3.8.x) makes it compatible with a closed-source INCDAW.

nodes.label: Audio Logger (60 s master ring buffer)
nodes.rationale: A ring buffer at the master node is cheap if designed in now and invasive later, so it was specified in AUDIO_ENGINE.md §8 during Phase 0.
nodes.norm_label: audio logger (60 s master ring buffer)

nodes.label: Phase 11 — Automation
nodes.rationale: Complete in two parts (11a the generic subsystem D-022, 11b placement and write-mode recording D-026). Exit criterion: any parameter registered in the parameter system is automatable with no parameter-specific code, tested by registering an unknown key and automating it through the compiled graph.

nodes.label: Phase 12 — Recording and Audio Editor
nodes.rationale: Eight parts: WAV codec, wait-free input capture on a second IOProc (D-023), TimelineAnchor placement (D-024), the disk streamer under seqlocks with starvation as counted silence (D-025), the audio editor, input monitoring, loop/punch recording, and the Audio Logger. Exit criterion — a measured loopback landing sample-accurately with device latency applied — is asserted deterministically and re-verified on real hardware.

nodes.label: Phase 13 — Plugin Hosting
nodes.rationale: CLAP → AU → VST3 per PLUGIN_HOST.md, with vendored CLAP 1.2.6 (D-027) and the out-of-process incdaw-pluginscan. Exit criterion: real third-party plugins load and process and the deliberate misbehaviour matrix passes — a crashing plugin does not take down INCDAW and does not lose the project.

nodes.label: Phase 14 — Sampler
nodes.rationale: Exit criterion: a multisampled instrument plays correctly across the keyboard with velocity layers, streaming from disk without underruns.

nodes.label: Remaining Work by Gate
nodes.rationale: Sorted by what blocks each item rather than by feature area: dependency approval (AU, VST3, FLAC, MP3), platform/hardware (MIDI output, clock/sync, feedback, hot-plug), its own program (sandboxed plugin processing), and ungated future increments.

nodes.label: Plugin Misbehaviour Matrix
nodes.rationale: Deliberately hostile test plugins that crash on process, hang on load, return NaN, report absurd latency, allocate on the audio thread and fail state restore. INCDAW must survive every one with the project intact; real third-party plugins supplement it with real-world integration testing.

nodes.label: INCDAW Plugin Host
nodes.rationale: Plugin hosting is a major subsystem targeted at Phase 13; the document is written at Phase 0 as design-only so the host ABI can be designed for out-of-process hosting before any code exists.

nodes.label: Plugin Crash Policy
nodes.rationale: A watchdog detects a dead plugin process; the node becomes a silent pass-through, the user is notified, the project stays open and the last-known state is retained for reload. Losing a session to someone else's bug is not acceptable.

nodes.label: Out-of-Process Isolation Strategy
nodes.rationale: Retrofitting isolation into an in-process design means rewriting the host, so the boundary is drawn from the first line: audio crosses through a shared-memory ring buffer, parameters/state/events cross as serialisable messages, and no raw pointers into INCDAW's address space are exposed. In-process hosting is then a degenerate case and sandboxing later is configuration, not redesign.

nodes.label: VST2 Exclusion
nodes.rationale: Steinberg ended VST2 SDK licensing in 2018; there is no lawful path for a new closed-source product. This is the single deliberate divergence from the FL Studio 2026 macOS format list.

nodes.label: Automated Layering Test
nodes.rationale: Written in Phase 1 before any engine code so that layering rules are enforced mechanically from the first commit instead of being a documented aspiration.

nodes.label: Denormal Handling (FTZ/DAZ at callback entry)
nodes.rationale: Denormals disabled on arm64 via FPCR at callback entry because untreated denormals cause large, mysterious CPU spikes on decaying tails.

nodes.label: Realtime Safety Guard (debug builds)
nodes.rationale: Design intent is not enough; the rule must be mechanically checked. Entering the callback sets a thread-local flag and an overridden global operator new/delete plus instrumented lock acquisition assert if it is set, so any allocation or lock on the audio path fails the suite in CI on the commit that introduced it. Also bans shared_ptr copies, std::function construction, exceptions across the boundary, node-based containers, and any syscall or logging.

nodes.label: P7 — Time-Stretch / Pitch Subsystem (WSOLA, transient-aware)
nodes.rationale: DONE. engine::dsp::timeStretch (WSOLA with shared-channel alignment and transient locking so clicks survive both directions exactly once; pitch via stretch plus windowed-sinc; exact identity at 1.0/0). StretchAssetCommand gives bit-exact undo of the file; StretchClipsCommand plus Option-drag at the clip edge implements FL's resize-vs-stretch distinction; warped clips render offline at compile time.

nodes.label: Time Stretching / Pitch Shifting Gap
nodes.rationale: Identified as the single largest functional gap against FL Studio — absent from playlist clips, audio editor and sampler alike; a low-quality placeholder explicitly does not count as closure.

nodes.label: Performance Instrumentation (callback histogram, per-node timing, underrun counter)
nodes.rationale: Built in Phase 2 alongside the engine so no later phase optimises blind. A histogram (p50/p95/p99/max) rather than an average, plus audio-thread allocation count which must be zero.
nodes.norm_label: performance instrumentation (callback histogram, per-node timing, underrun counter)

nodes.label: Table-Driven Resampler Kernel Optimisation
nodes.rationale: The resampler evaluated sinc and a 4-term window per tap per frame — two transcendental calls x 64 taps x every output sample. Replaced by a 512-phase x 64-tap precomputed table per resample call with linear interpolation between phase rows; phase-interpolation error sits far below the window's own -92 dB sidelobes and the quality regression test passes unchanged. 547.9 ms to 18.6 ms, 29x faster.

nodes.label: Headless Deterministic Framework-Free Core
nodes.rationale: The core must compile and pass its full test suite with no UI, no CoreAudio and no plugin SDK linked. Chosen because the parts that are hard to get right (timing, routing, serialization, automation) are also the cheapest to test, and they must never depend on the parts that are expensive to test. Anything untestable headlessly is excluded from the core by definition.

nodes.label: Downward-Only Layer Model (ui/app/project/engine/plugins/platform)
nodes.rationale: Dependencies point downward only; a layer may use anything below it and must know nothing above it. engine/ never references ui/ or app/, macOS symbols live only in platform/, dsp/ never allocates, serialization lives only in project/. Rules are made load-bearing rather than aspirational by writing the layering test in Phase 1 before any engine code.

nodes.label: Audio Thread Prime Directive
nodes.rationale: The audio thread never allocates, never locks, never performs I/O, never waits on the UI, and never performs an operation whose duration it cannot bound. Everything else in the audio engine design is stated as a consequence of that one sentence.

nodes.label: D-001 — Core implementation language: C++20
nodes.rationale: Chosen C++20 with Apple clang 21 over Rust, Swift and Web Audio: the only ecosystem where CLAP, AU and VST3 are natively consumable without an FFI shim, with explicit control over allocation, threading and memory layout in the audio path. Tradeoff: no language-level memory safety, mitigated by the testing strategy, the realtime guard and strict ownership rules. Status ACCEPTED, 2026-08-14.

nodes.label: D-025 — Streaming is a window, and starving it is audible, not fatal
nodes.rationale: Each streamed clip owns two ~1.4 s segments; a seek-negotiating ring would be more machinery for the same guarantee, and an underfed window should degrade audibly rather than block the callback.
nodes.norm_label: d-025 — streaming is a window, and starving it is audible, not fatal

nodes.label: Measure-First Optimisation Method
nodes.rationale: Measure, find the actual hot path by profiling, optimise only the measured bottleneck, re-measure and record before/after in the commit message, guard with a regression test. Optimisations without a recorded measurement are rejected in review regardless of how obviously correct they seem.

nodes.label: RenderGraph (compiled immutable graph)
nodes.rationale: The engine consumes a compiled, immutable, topologically sorted, latency-compensated graph rather than the project model. Compilation on a background thread performs cycle detection, topological sort, latency accumulation for PDC, buffer allocation and node parameter binding; the audio thread receives a finished read-only object.

nodes.label: AudioClipNode
nodes.rationale: A timeline-reading node: produces nothing while the transport is stopped, otherwise it loops a few hundred frames of clip forever.

nodes.label: AutomationNode
nodes.rationale: Keeps evaluating while the transport is stopped: holding a parked playhead's parameter values is what makes the mixer show where the playhead actually is.

nodes.label: InstrumentNode
nodes.rationale: Reads the timeline, so it produces no sequenced notes while stopped. It ends its sequenced notes once, on the first stopped block, and then leaves the instrument alone: a keyboard played into a parked project is the normal way an instrument is auditioned, and killing voices every block turns a held note into a buzz.

nodes.label: Offline Rendering Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Only permitted differences from realtime: the driving loop is not device-paced, plugins are told they render offline where the format supports it, and higher-quality resampling/stretching modes may be selected as a documented user-visible choice. If the byte-identity regression test cannot pass, the architecture is wrong and must be fixed rather than the test relaxed.

nodes.label: ProcessContext::playing
nodes.rationale: The flag every node receives so timeline-reading nodes fall silent while parked, while nodes carrying sound of their own keep rendering. Without it a node re-emits the window under the playhead every block — a note retriggered at block rate, or a few hundred frames of clip looped forever — heard as a hum that starts with the application and never stops.

nodes.label: Transport (single clock authority)
nodes.rationale: MIDI scheduling, audio clip playback, automation evaluation and offline rendering all read the same sample position from the same object; there is no second clock anywhere in the system. A stopped transport still renders (a synth's release, a delay tail, input monitoring must keep coming out) so processBlock keeps returning one segment while stopped, carrying the same playPosition on every block because the timeline is parked.

nodes.label: P3 — Playlist Clip Split, Timeline Markers and Regions
nodes.rationale: DONE. SplitClipCommand is tick-exact for pattern/automation clips and frame-exact for audio, with source offsets advancing; TimelineMarker model plus project format v1.5 and MarkerCommands; Option-click slices, M / Shift+M drop a marker or one-bar region at the playhead.
nodes.norm_label: p3 — playlist clip split, timeline markers and regions

nodes.label: Offline/Realtime Render Equivalence
nodes.rationale: Offline render uses the same RenderGraph and the same node implementations as realtime playback. Not an optimisation — the only way to guarantee that what you export is what you heard, verified by an automated byte-equivalence test.

nodes.label: Sample-Accurate Block Splitting at Event Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Nodes split the block at event boundaries rather than quantising events to block starts. This is the difference between a DAW that is sample-accurate and one that merely claims to be, and it must be true from the first note in Phase 5 because it cannot be added later without touching every node. Loop boundaries and tempo changes reuse the same mechanism instead of special cases.
nodes.norm_label: sample-accurate block splitting at event boundaries

nodes.label: D-013 — Pattern and automation clips are placed in ticks, audio clips in frames
nodes.rationale: Both time bases are kept because the two clip kinds genuinely have different ones: musical material follows the tempo map, recorded audio follows the sample clock.
nodes.norm_label: d-013 — pattern and automation clips are placed in ticks, audio clips in frames

nodes.label: D-022 — Automation is a registry plus a node, evaluated per block
nodes.rationale: A ParameterRegistry mapping key to how a normalised value lands on a target, evaluated by a node on the audio path, because a UI timer stops automating when the window is busy and knows nothing about offline render.
nodes.norm_label: d-022 — automation is a registry plus a node, evaluated per block

nodes.label: D-026 — Automation placement is a window over a lane
nodes.rationale: AutomationNode::Binding carries a half-open tick window; not writing outside the window gives clip semantics for free.
nodes.norm_label: d-026 — automation placement is a window over a lane

nodes.label: macOS Audio Workgroups API Finding
nodes.rationale: FL Studio 2026 adopting Audio Workgroups for audio-thread scheduling is independent validation of decision D-004 — a shipping professional DAW made the same call on the same hardware class.

nodes.label: FL Studio 2026 Functional Reference
nodes.rationale: Capabilities and workflows are reproduced, never implementation, source, assets, presets, branding or visual identity (CLAUDE.md §43). Findings were drawn from Image-Line's official release page and online manual during Phase 0 discovery — not from memory and not from inspecting the local installation.

nodes.label: Separate Input and Output Device Selectors
nodes.rationale: Because the reference gained separate selectors, INCDAW's device layer must not assume a single duplex device.
nodes.norm_label: separate input and output device selectors

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Audio Engine Foundation
nodes.rationale: CoreAudio device layer, os_workgroup-joined realtime thread, lock-free SPSC queues and reaper, realtime-safety guard, RenderGraph, callback histogram. Exit criterion: a sine reaches the output with zero underruns over a 60-minute soak and zero allocations/locks on the audio thread.

nodes.label: 60-Minute Soak Test
nodes.rationale: Asserts zero underruns, no memory growth and a callback duration histogram within budget over an hour of continuous playback — the only way slow leaks and rare spikes surface.

nodes.label: Test Levels (unit, integration, end-to-end)
nodes.rationale: The end-to-end path runs as one scripted test through the command registry, which is possible precisely because every action is a command — the testing strategy depends on the architecture decision.

nodes.label: INCDAW Requirements
nodes.rationale: Records what INCDAW must eventually do and what the functional reference actually does; it is the source document for phase planning in the roadmap.

nodes.label: INCDAW Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Phases follow CLAUDE.md §37 and each has a testable exit criterion: a phase is not complete because code exists or compiles, but because its criterion passes. A phase that has not met its criterion does not advance.

nodes.label: INCDAW Testing Strategy
nodes.rationale: The standing contract each phase built against; at Phase 19 the live suite is 483 cases and ~1.34M assertions, green in Debug and Release.

nodes.label: Scriptable Command Surface Evidence
nodes.rationale: FL's assistant can organise tracks, route mixer channels, set levels, adjust plugin parameters and generate Piano Roll content only because FL exposes a scriptable command surface — strong support for INCDAW's command-registry-from-day-one decision.

nodes.label: Testable Exit Criterion
nodes.rationale: The device that keeps the roadmap honest — each phase names a measurable pass/fail condition, so 'done' cannot be claimed for code that merely compiles or a UI that merely shows something.

nodes.label: Definition of Done Principle
nodes.rationale: A feature is done when its behaviour is proven by a test that would fail if the behaviour regressed — not because it compiles or the UI shows something. Two literal consequences: every serious bug gets a permanent regression test, and the core is testable headlessly with no UI, device or plugins.

nodes.label: Theme (single drawn design language for the shell)
nodes.rationale: src/ui/macos/Theme.{h,mm} is the shell's only palette and drawing vocabulary (D-035); no view declares a colour of its own.
nodes.norm_label: theme (single drawn design language for the shell)

nodes.label: DelayLineNode
nodes.rationale: Inserted on edges that would arrive early, sized to the difference, and reports its own latency so recomputed arrival times are equal by construction.

nodes.label: engine::GraphBuilder::compile
nodes.rationale: Where delay compensation lives (D-019), because it already computed the longest path to every node; it also exposes the total as CompiledGraph::latencyFrames() for the UI and the recording path.

nodes.label: Plugin Delay Compensation
nodes.rationale: Latency accumulated at graph-compile time, not runtime: each node reports latency, the compiler computes the longest path, and DelayLineNodes are inserted on early-arriving edges. Delay lines report their own latency so one pass suffices. Compensation can be disabled so MixerTests can assert both that a latent path aligns and that it smears into two impulses without it — a PDC test that passes either way is testing nothing.

nodes.label: Phase 18 Measured Baseline (2026-08-16)
nodes.rationale: Graph rebuild 0.049 ms at 16 channels and 0.158 ms at 64; offline render 63x realtime; builtin effects 0.2-8.6 ns/frame; resample 10 s 48->44.1 kHz at 547.9 ms. Reading: rebuild and the realtime path have headroom everywhere, so optimising there is unjustified (CLAUDE.md §27). Deliberately not optimised: rebuild latency, builtin effects, the Sampler's gated per-frame LFO/filter path, and UI frame profiling that would require Xcode.

nodes.label: EQ Benchmark Flaw (midpoint parameters measured a bypass)
nodes.rationale: The benchmark set parameters to range midpoints; the EQ's mid gain midpoint is 0 dB, which the effect skips as identity — so the reported 0.2 ns/frame was the cost of a bypass. Fixed by setting parameters to 75% of range; honest cost 15.6 ns/frame, 0.07% of budget, no optimisation needed. A measurement that silently measures nothing is worse than no measurement.
nodes.norm_label: eq benchmark flaw (midpoint parameters measured a bypass)

nodes.label: incdaw-bench (tools/bench)
nodes.rationale: Committed so every published number is reproducible with ./build/incdaw-bench. Medians over 20 runs for compile, single runs for throughput; block-cost lines average 4,000 blocks.

nodes.label: Viewport Culling in Metal-Rendered Editors
nodes.rationale: Only visible notes and clips are drawn — required to hit 10,000 notes at 60 fps. Measured at 0.012 ms/frame against a 16.6 ms budget.

nodes.label: D-006 — UI: AppKit shell + INCDAW-owned Metal-rendered widget layer
nodes.rationale: A native AppKit window and menu bar hosting an INCDAW-owned widget layer, chosen because the two most important editors require custom rendering anyway; a full third-party UI framework would be carried for the parts that need it least.
nodes.norm_label: d-006 — ui: appkit shell + incdaw-owned metal-rendered widget layer

nodes.label: D-015 — The Channel Rack is drawn with CoreGraphics, not Metal
nodes.rationale: CoreGraphics for the rack and pattern list, Metal kept for the Piano Roll: the two have genuinely different budgets — a rack draws a few dozen rectangles and mostly text, the Piano Roll must cull ten thousand notes inside a frame. Rendering is chosen per pane by measurement, not by policy.
nodes.norm_label: d-015 — the channel rack is drawn with coregraphics, not metal

nodes.label: D-019 — Delay compensation lives in the graph compiler
nodes.rationale: GraphBuilder::compile already computed the longest path to every node; alignment is a property of the graph, not of the mixer, so putting it anywhere else duplicates the traversal and misses non-mixer latency.
nodes.norm_label: d-019 — delay compensation lives in the graph compiler

nodes.label: D-035 — One drawn design language for the shell: FL Studio's density, GarageBand's calm
nodes.rationale: src/ui/macos/Theme.{h,mm} plus shared drawing helpers, because a palette alone does not stop two panes from drawing the same control differently. Adopting a third-party UI kit was rejected for the reason D-006 already gives. The Metal instancing performance model is untouched: a pane still draws one instance per element in one draw call.
nodes.norm_label: d-035 — one drawn design language for the shell: fl studio's density, garageband's calm

nodes.label: P10 — Audio Unit Hosting (effects)
nodes.rationale: DONE for effects. platform::AudioUnitHost enumerates components without running plugin code and renders stereo float in-place through AudioUnitRender, behind a header containing no CoreAudio type. plugins::HostedPlugin became the interface PluginNode, the instance manager, PDC, state files and editor windows are written against, with ClapInstance and AudioUnitInstance as its two implementations, so AUs appear in Add Insert without a scan. Not included: AU instruments, custom Cocoa views, out-of-process instantiation. Chosen because it uses a system API and adds no dependency.
nodes.community_name: D-007 — Plugin format support: CLAP, AU, VST3 (VST2 excluded)

nodes.label: os_signpost Profiling (Instruments.app unavailable)
nodes.rationale: Added in Phase 2 and usable from the command line. Instruments.app requires full Xcode, which is not installed; installing it becomes a dependency decision only if deep GPU or system-level profiling proves necessary in Phase 18, and this document does not assume it.
nodes.community_name: D-007 — Plugin format support: CLAP, AU, VST3 (VST2 excluded)

nodes.label: D-002 — Build system: CMake + Ninja
nodes.rationale: CMake >= 3.28 driving Ninja, chosen over Meson, Bazel and hand-written Makefiles because it works fully with Command Line Tools alone (no Xcode.app) and carries forward to the eventual Windows target (D-005). Status ACCEPTED, with installation of the tools themselves still pending approval.
nodes.community_name: D-007 — Plugin format support: CLAP, AU, VST3 (VST2 excluded)

nodes.label: D-003 — Audio I/O: CoreAudio HAL directly, no wrapper framework
nodes.rationale: CoreAudio HAL behind an INCDAW-owned AudioDevice interface. AVAudioEngine imposes its own graph and node model, which conflicts with INCDAW's compiled RenderGraph; the owned interface is also what makes the later Windows target (D-005) a port rather than a rewrite.
nodes.community_name: D-007 — Plugin format support: CLAP, AU, VST3 (VST2 excluded)
nodes.norm_label: d-003 — audio i/o: coreaudio hal directly, no wrapper framework

nodes.label: D-005 — Platform strategy: macOS first, Windows later, Linux not precluded
nodes.rationale: macOS/arm64 is the only build target for Phases 1-20 because shipping one platform properly beats shipping two badly; platform-specific code stays isolated so a later port is a port.
nodes.community_name: D-007 — Plugin format support: CLAP, AU, VST3 (VST2 excluded)
nodes.norm_label: d-005 — platform strategy: macos first, windows later, linux not precluded

nodes.label: D-007 — Plugin format support: CLAP, AU, VST3 (VST2 excluded)
nodes.rationale: Implement CLAP then AU then VST3. VST2 is excluded because its licensing would otherwise conflict with D-008's closed-source position.
nodes.community_name: D-007 — Plugin format support: CLAP, AU, VST3 (VST2 excluded)
nodes.norm_label: d-007 — plugin format support: clap, au, vst3 (vst2 excluded)

nodes.label: D-008 — Licensing: INCDAW is closed-source
nodes.rationale: Closed-source with permissive dependencies only (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0). Copyleft frameworks are avoided partly because what they would provide (device I/O, AU hosting) is already available natively via D-003 and D-007.
nodes.community_name: D-007 — Plugin format support: CLAP, AU, VST3 (VST2 excluded)

nodes.label: D-011 — Metal shaders are compiled at runtime, not built offline
nodes.rationale: Compile from an embedded source string once during startup. Removes an 8 GB Xcode toolchain dependency (only Command Line Tools are installed, per D-002) for what is a one-time startup cost.
nodes.community_name: D-007 — Plugin format support: CLAP, AU, VST3 (VST2 excluded)
nodes.norm_label: d-011 — metal shaders are compiled at runtime, not built offline

nodes.label: D-027 — CLAP SDK vendored, pinned at 1.2.6
nodes.rationale: The chosen format order stands per D-007: CLAP first because it has the cleanest ABI and needs no SDK build.
nodes.community_name: D-007 — Plugin format support: CLAP, AU, VST3 (VST2 excluded)
nodes.norm_label: d-027 — clap sdk vendored, pinned at 1.2.6

nodes.label: D-031 — Plugin instances live for their slot's lifetime, not the graph's
nodes.rationale: The slot IS the user-facing identity of 'this plugin here', so an instance must survive graph rebuilds along with its internal state and editor.
nodes.community_name: D-007 — Plugin format support: CLAP, AU, VST3 (VST2 excluded)
nodes.norm_label: d-031 — plugin instances live for their slot's lifetime, not the graph's

nodes.label: D-032 — Decoded samples are cached by file identity, not held by persistent samplers
nodes.rationale: engine::SampleCache owned by the application, because the expensive thing is the decode, not the sampler object. Explicitly distinguished from D-031, which solved a different problem: a plugin instance carries state, a decoded sample does not.
nodes.community_name: D-007 — Plugin format support: CLAP, AU, VST3 (VST2 excluded)
nodes.norm_label: d-032 — decoded samples are cached by file identity, not held by persistent samplers

nodes.label: Product Decision: No Cloud Services or Bundled Commercial Content
nodes.rationale: FL Cloud backup, Loop Starter content and subscriptions are excluded by recorded product decision (REQUIREMENTS §1.3), alongside VST2.
nodes.community_name: D-007 — Plugin format support: CLAP, AU, VST3 (VST2 excluded)
nodes.norm_label: product decision: no cloud services or bundled commercial content

nodes.label: tools/make-dmg.sh
nodes.rationale: Builds its own Release tree (build-release/), ad-hoc signs the bundle, verifies the signature and produces dist/INCDAW-<version>.dmg.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — Research and Architecture
nodes.rationale: Repository, environment, architecture and FL Studio functional-reference discovery; stack decisions D-001…D-010. Exit criterion — stack approved by the user — met 2026-08-14.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Foundation and Build System
nodes.rationale: The DMG pipeline is built here rather than in Phase 20 so packaging is exercised continuously and never becomes a late surprise. Includes the layering test that fails the build if engine/ references ui/ or macOS symbols escape platform/.

nodes.label: Phase 20 — Release Engineering
nodes.rationale: Exit criterion: a team member installs from the DMG on a different Mac and launches INCDAW successfully by the documented procedure — the release is proven by someone else's machine, not the build machine.

nodes.label: doctest Framework
nodes.rationale: Chosen (D-008) for compile speed, zero build complexity, and an MIT license compatible with closed-source INCDAW; Catch2 (BSL-1.0) is an acceptable alternative.

nodes.label: Layering Test
nodes.rationale: A static check that engine/ never references ui/ or app/, that macOS and platform symbols appear only in platform/, and that no layer cycles exist — this is what turns ARCHITECTURE.md §2 from a document into a constraint. It is also currently the only thing protecting Windows portability, and explicitly not a substitute for compiling.

nodes.label: INCDAW Release Process
nodes.rationale: A release is one ad-hoc-signed DMG built from a clean tree whose whole suite is green in Debug and Release; live for 0.9.0 (Phase 20).

nodes.label: Ad-Hoc Signing Instead of Notarization (D-009)
nodes.rationale: INCDAW has no Developer ID enrolment, so the DMG is ad-hoc signed — a real signature, because arm64 refuses to execute unsigned binaries — but Gatekeeper quarantines any copy that arrives over a network, requiring a one-time right-click-Open or xattr -dr per downloaded copy.

nodes.label: Out-of-Scope Product Decisions
nodes.rationale: Cloud storage/backup, bundled commercial content libraries and AI assistant features are excluded as product decisions, not architectural gaps.

nodes.label: Deliberately Out of Scope
nodes.rationale: VST2 hosting (not licensable, D-007), notarized public distribution (no Developer ID, D-009), Windows builds (future target kept possible by platform/ isolation, D-005), cloud/collaboration, and bundled commercial sample content.

nodes.label: Plugin Editor / UI Bridge
nodes.rationale: CLAP_EXT_GUI is driven create → set_scale → get_size → set_parent → show with no editor left behind on any refusal, and the destructor closes an open editor first so a closing window and a dying instance cannot double-free. The parent view crosses the layer as void* so plugins/ never includes Cocoa. Editor code never runs on the audio thread and the audio thread never waits on an editor.

nodes.label: Autosave, Backup and Crash Recovery (history/)
nodes.rationale: Snapshots are written on an interval and before risky operations (migration, plugin scan, bounce) and rotated with a configurable retention count; backup filenames embed the save date, which FL Studio 2026 also does and which is the difference between a usable and unusable backup folder. Autosave is always a separate file and never overwrites the user's own save.

nodes.label: Increment 11 — Settings, MIDI In, Command Search
nodes.rationale: settings.json is its own versioned file, never project data (D-036); the status line reads back from the OPEN device rather than from the request. Opening platform::MidiDevice in the shell closed the gap that had made engine::MidiInput unreachable from hardware since Phase 5, and Command Search exposed a registry table that was empty in the running application until now. Undo/redo route through one shell path and name what they will do (D-037).
nodes.norm_label: increment 11 — settings, midi in, command search

nodes.label: Increment 1 — Project Lifecycle Safety
nodes.rationale: Dirty tracking, quit/open/new guard, autosave with crash recovery, Open Recent. Headless decisions live in app/ProjectSession and are tested; only interaction lives in the shell. Exit criterion met: a crash loses at most the autosave interval.

nodes.label: Increment 2 — Generic Insert Parameter Panel
nodes.rationale: Open Editor always opens something — a hosted plugin's own GUI, or the generic panel built from the builtin catalogue or CLAP discovery, writing through the same ParameterSink a lane automates. Builtin instrument parameters were deliberately deferred to increment 4 because instruments have sinks but no StateIO, so a panel value would silently vanish at save/load.

nodes.label: Increment 3 — Export Options Dialog
nodes.rationale: Fronts everything project::OfflineRender already implemented; exit criterion is that every RenderOptions field is reachable from the dialog and multi-file targets land without overwriting each other (app::session::exportFileName, tested).

nodes.label: UI Build-Out (post-phase increments)
nodes.rationale: Authorised 2026-08-16: FL-Studio-class workspaces over the finished engine, in increments held to the same discipline as the phases but without renumbering them. It binds to a surface that already exists — CompiledProjectGraph handles, the command registry, ParameterRegistry, MIDI learn plumbing, the offline renderer, SMF exchange, the sample cache.

nodes.label: Event-Based Parameter Delivery (ParameterSink)
nodes.rationale: setParameter pushes onto a preallocated lock-free queue that process() drains into the block's clap_event_param_value input list at block start. Delivery by event rather than by a call into the plugin makes the CLAP concurrency contract (no flush during processing) unviolatable by construction.

nodes.label: params->flush() Recorded As Not Currently Applicable
nodes.rationale: Every write path (panel, automation, MIDI map) resolves through the compiled graph, and a slot without a live node has no sink, so a value can never sit in the queue of an instance whose process() is not running. The case returns only if a future surface writes to a BYPASSED slot's persisted instance directly — implement flush then, not before (2026-08-16).
nodes.norm_label: params->flush() recorded as not currently applicable

nodes.label: What Is Not Tested Automatically
nodes.rationale: Audio quality judgements, hosted plugin editor rendering, device-specific behaviour and Windows are stated as gaps because honesty matters more than coverage theatre — so no one later mistakes a green suite for proof they were covered.

nodes.label: Atomic Graph Pointer Swap
nodes.rationale: The graph the audio thread reads is immutable while being read. Edits build a new graph on a background thread and hand it over by atomic pointer swap; the old graph goes to the reaper. This avoids any lock or in-place mutation on the realtime path, including when a plugin changes its reported latency.

nodes.label: Lock-Free SPSC Command Queue (UI to Audio, Audio to UI)
nodes.rationale: Messages are POD or hold pre-allocated pointers so the audio thread never constructs anything. Audio-to-UI drops are acceptable for anything the UI can re-derive, which removes any need for backpressure on the realtime side.
nodes.norm_label: lock-free spsc command queue (ui to audio, audio to ui)

nodes.label: Reaper Queue (off-thread destruction)
nodes.rationale: Objects the audio thread stops using are pushed to a reaper queue and destroyed on a background thread, because the audio thread must never call a destructor that frees memory.

nodes.label: AudioCaptureSink (atomic capture sink pointer)
nodes.rationale: The engine forwards captured blocks through one atomic sink pointer — explicitly the capture twin of the graph swap — so the capture path crosses the realtime boundary with the same lock-free handover discipline as the render graph.

nodes.label: AudioIOCallback::captureAudioBlock
nodes.rationale: Input is its own clock domain with its own IOProc (a duplex device reuses the main proc's input arguments); each captured block carries the HAL's input timestamp. Whoever places the audio subtracts totalInputLatencyFrames, and the loopback tests prove the subtraction is real by asserting its absence misaligns by exactly the reported latency.

nodes.label: Four-Class Threading Model
nodes.rationale: Audio (RT), Worker (RT), UI and Background threads, with crossings only via the listed mechanisms. RT classes may neither allocate nor block; mutexes shared with the audio thread, shared_ptr refcount traffic on the audio thread, and 'just this once' blocking are forbidden outright.

nodes.label: D-023 — Capture is a second clock domain, reconciled by timestamps
nodes.rationale: A second IOProc on the input device rather than an aggregate device: aggregates hide the clock problem without solving it and force a device the user did not choose.
nodes.norm_label: d-023 — capture is a second clock domain, reconciled by timestamps

nodes.label: D-024 — A take is placed by clock correlation, not by counting
nodes.rationale: The engine publishes a TimelineAnchor from every rendered block, because counting blocks breaks the moment a block is split by a loop or a tempo change.
nodes.norm_label: d-024 — a take is placed by clock correlation, not by counting

nodes.label: Design-Level Performance Decisions
nodes.rationale: Settled early because they are expensive to change later: graph compiled off the audio thread, Metal editors with viewport culling, lock-free queues only across the realtime boundary, buffers preallocated at compile, disk streaming for large samples, lazy media/plugin-state loading, persistent plugin registry so startup never rescans, denormals disabled, and os_workgroup membership for all realtime threads (D-004).

nodes.label: Insert Chain Compilation (inserts -> fader -> pan -> mute -> outputs)
nodes.rationale: Insert nodes are built by an injected factory (D-028) so the compiler places engine::Nodes and never learns what a plugin is — which is also what lets Phase 15 built-in effects be inserts without being plugins.
nodes.community_name: D-028 — Hosted plugins reach the graph through an injected factory
nodes.norm_label: insert chain compilation (inserts -> fader -> pan -> mute -> outputs)

nodes.label: MixerStripNode and the compiled mixer
nodes.rationale: Every MixerNode becomes a MixerStripNode and RoutingConnections become edges (a send is an edge carrying its own gain node). Each channel gets its own strip so channel volume and pan use the same arithmetic the mixer does. Signal path: instrument -> channel strip -> mixer track -> sends/buses -> master; a routing cycle is refused by the graph builder rather than broken arbitrarily.
nodes.community_name: D-028 — Hosted plugins reach the graph through an injected factory

nodes.label: P4 — Functional Sidechain Routing (compressor external key input)
nodes.rationale: DONE. Sidechain edges compile into detector-only inputs on the destination's compressor inserts, PDC-aligned like any other edge, with the key never summing into audio; mixer strip menu gained 'Sidechain Into'. Previously the edges serialized but compiled to nothing.
nodes.community_name: D-028 — Hosted plugins reach the graph through an injected factory
nodes.norm_label: p4 — functional sidechain routing (compressor external key input)

nodes.label: P5 — LUFS Meter (EBU R128), Stereo Separation, True Pre-Fader Sends
nodes.rationale: DONE. incdaw.loudness insert with BS.1770-4 K-weighting designed per rate, momentary/short-term/gated-integrated via histogram, calibrated to the -3.01 LUFS reference at 44.1 and 48 kHz; mid/side stereo separation on every strip (model, format, command and automation key); pre-fader sends tap ahead of the fader through a spliced unity node.
nodes.community_name: D-028 — Hosted plugins reach the graph through an injected factory
nodes.norm_label: p5 — lufs meter (ebu r128), stereo separation, true pre-fader sends

nodes.label: P6 — Chorus, Flanger, Phaser and Transient/Sustain Splitter
nodes.rationale: DONE. incdaw.chorus/flanger/phaser (LFO delay, comb, allpass; bit-exact null at defaults) and incdaw.transientsplit (fast/slow envelope race with both/transients/sustain outputs so parallel strips shape each half, exact-unity reassembly). FL 2026 Transmitter equivalent.
nodes.community_name: D-028 — Hosted plugins reach the graph through an injected factory
nodes.norm_label: p6 — chorus, flanger, phaser and transient/sustain splitter

nodes.label: D-028 — Hosted plugins reach the graph through an injected factory
nodes.rationale: The pattern already established for instruments; it keeps the compiler placing engine::Nodes without ever learning what a plugin is.
nodes.community_name: D-028 — Hosted plugins reach the graph through an injected factory
nodes.norm_label: d-028 — hosted plugins reach the graph through an injected factory

nodes.label: D-029 — Plugin parameters automate through a sink target and an event queue
nodes.rationale: Keeps the ParameterRegistry the single place where per-parameter knowledge lives, and lets a new plugin format arrive without the factory signature changing and without engine/ knowing what a CLAP is (D-028).
nodes.community_name: D-028 — Hosted plugins reach the graph through an injected factory
nodes.norm_label: d-029 — plugin parameters automate through a sink target and an event queue

nodes.label: D-030 — Plugin state travels as blob files inside the package
nodes.rationale: It is the package's own design — a corrupted pattern costs one pattern — and it mirrors D-029's ParameterSink: a pure interface in engine/, implemented outside it.
nodes.community_name: D-028 — Hosted plugins reach the graph through an injected factory
nodes.norm_label: d-030 — plugin state travels as blob files inside the package

nodes.label: D-033 — Builtin effects are inserts with the plugin identity, built by the compiler
nodes.rationale: The exit criterion literally forbids special-casing builtin effects, so they take the same insert identity and the same compiler path as hosted plugins.
nodes.community_name: D-028 — Hosted plugins reach the graph through an injected factory
nodes.norm_label: d-033 — builtin effects are inserts with the plugin identity, built by the compiler

nodes.label: app::AppSettings::audio (device configuration)
nodes.rationale: Read from settings.json before anything touches hardware (D-036). Defaults are system default output at 48 kHz / 512 frames — 512 rather than the hardware minimum because the block size is set on the SHARED device and Bluetooth output crackles below it. Input is opt-in because opening the microphone unasked is a permission prompt nobody requested. Reported figures are read back from the OPEN device, never from the request, since the granted figure is the only honest latency number; a device that refuses to open falls back to the system default so a wrong preference never costs a session.

nodes.label: AudioDevice (platform device interface)
nodes.rationale: Backed by CoreAudio HAL directly (D-003) behind an INCDAW-owned interface in platform/. Buffer frame size, safety offset, latency, nominal sample rate and the IO thread workgroup must be read and honoured, not guessed — reported latency is what makes recorded audio land in the right place, and getting it wrong is silent and discovered much later.

nodes.label: Audio Logger (60-second master ring buffer)
