nodes.rationale: Architecturally trivial if designed in now (one ring write at the master node, one background drain) and invasive if bolted on later, so it was specified in Phase 0 and implemented in Phase 12. ~23 MB resident at 48 kHz stereo float32 — acceptable. grab snapshots the monotonic write count, copies, and trims whatever the writer overran, so a grab is never torn and never takes a lock near the callback. Off by default because the memory and the 'was that being kept?' question belong to the user.

nodes.label: FL Studio 2026 Gap Analysis (INCDAW 0.9.0)
nodes.rationale: Baseline INCDAW 0.9.0 (phases 0-20 complete), dated 2026-08-16, measured against Image-Line's official release page and online manual. FL Studio is a functional reference for capabilities and workflows only — never implementation, assets or branding (CLAUDE.md §43).

nodes.label: os_workgroup Realtime Thread Scheduling
nodes.rationale: Additional realtime workers must join the device workgroup via kAudioDevicePropertyIOThreadOSWorkgroup and os_workgroup_join / os_workgroup_interval_start; auxiliary realtime work uses AudioWorkIntervalCreate. Without this, workers on an Apple M5 can be scheduled onto efficiency cores and cause underruns that appear random and are extremely hard to diagnose.

nodes.label: Separate Input and Output Device Selection
nodes.rationale: FL Studio 2026's release notes record adding separate macOS input/output selectors and the same need applies here. The device layer must not assume one duplex device and must handle the aggregate/mismatched-clock case explicitly rather than by accident.
nodes.norm_label: separate input and output device selection

nodes.label: D-004 — Realtime thread scheduling: os_workgroup / Audio Workgroups
nodes.rationale: Join the device workgroup and create an interval workgroup via AudioWorkIntervalCreate: Apple's sanctioned mechanism for realtime audio on heterogeneous P/E-core Apple silicon, without which worker threads land on efficiency cores and produce apparently random underruns.
nodes.norm_label: d-004 — realtime thread scheduling: os_workgroup / audio workgroups

nodes.label: D-036 — Machine settings live in their own versioned file, never in the project
nodes.rationale: A project describes the music; settings describe the machine it is played on. Mixing them makes a project unopenable or wrongly configured on a different machine.
nodes.norm_label: d-036 — machine settings live in their own versioned file, never in the project

nodes.label: project::compileProjectGraph
nodes.rationale: Must live in project/ because engine/ sits below it and cannot see a Project — enforced by the layering test. Everything musical (polymetric repeats, swing, note probability) resolves during compilation, never on the audio thread; probability is rolled from a project-derived seed so a compile is reproducible and offline render produces the notes the user heard.

nodes.label: InstrumentFactory (injected)
nodes.rationale: Instruments are supplied by an injected factory so plugin hosting (Phase 13) becomes a different factory rather than a change to the compiler.

nodes.label: Pattern Mode and Song Mode
nodes.source_location: §7 Patterns, tracks and the two transport modes
nodes.rationale: The difference is decided when the project is compiled, never on the audio thread (D-017): pattern mode compiles one pattern and loops it, song mode compiles the arrangement and loops its length. A channel makes sound and a track holds placements — deliberately not the same axis, so one clip can sound on eight channels and one channel can sound from clips on several tracks.

nodes.label: D-014 — Swing displaces only notes exactly on the grid
nodes.rationale: A grid/8 tolerance was implemented and rejected: a tolerance width cannot be explained to the user and it silently moves notes the user placed deliberately off the grid.
nodes.norm_label: d-014 — swing displaces only notes exactly on the grid

nodes.label: D-017 — Pattern mode and song mode are a compile-time distinction
nodes.rationale: The mode selects PlaybackSource when the project is compiled, because a flag read on the audio thread means a branch in the hot path and a second source of truth about what is playing.
nodes.norm_label: d-017 — pattern mode and song mode are a compile-time distinction

nodes.label: D-018 — Track mute and solo are resolved when the arrangement compiles
nodes.rationale: Skip muted tracks at compile time exactly as channel mute already works: a muted track's notes are then never compiled, never scheduled and never rendered-then-multiplied-by-zero.
nodes.norm_label: d-018 — track mute and solo are resolved when the arrangement compiles

nodes.label: D-034 — Instrument parameter values live in the model, applied at compile
nodes.rationale: Model storage is the rule the mixer already follows, so instrument state serializes and undoes by the same mechanism as everything else.
nodes.norm_label: d-034 — instrument parameter values live in the model, applied at compile

nodes.label: engine/audio/AudioLogger (last 60 s of master)
nodes.rationale: A keep-NEWEST circle (the recorder's ring is keep-oldest) fed at the end of every rendered block, so a grab retrieves exactly what was heard. Off by default: 23 MB and a 'was that being kept?' question the user should answer, not inherit. An input-side pre-record buffer is deliberately separate so microphone audio is never kept while the user believes only playback is.

nodes.label: engine/audio/AudioRecorder
nodes.rationale: Wait-free interleave into an SPSC ring on the capture thread, polling writer thread draining to disk, whole-frame drops counted and reported, take start reported with the device's input latency subtracted exactly once at the reporting edge.

nodes.label: project/RecordingSession
nodes.rationale: Arm-to-placement coordinator that never mutates the Project: it returns a Placement. computeSlices keeps the capture one continuous file and cuts it against the loop it was recorded under, stacking each pass as a muted take ready for comping; punch is a placement decision over a continuous capture, not a capture gate.

nodes.label: engine::TimelineAnchor (D-024)
nodes.rationale: Every rendered block publishes its (host time, timeline frame) correlation through a seqlock; the audio thread never blocks and readers retry the rare torn read.

nodes.label: Capture is a second clock domain (D-023)
nodes.rationale: Input timestamps are the HAL's, with reported input latency subtracted ONLY at the reporting edge (the recorder's Take) — subtract it anywhere else and it is applied twice. There is no sample-rate conversion on capture: an input that cannot run at the granted output rate is refused with both rates named (Bluetooth HFP mics at 24 kHz hit this in practice). Two-device drift within a take is real, second-order and deliberately unhandled.
nodes.norm_label: capture is a second clock domain (d-023)

nodes.label: Unfinalized take probes as zero frames
nodes.rationale: The WAV header is written with zero sizes and patched on finalize, so a crash mid-recording probes as an empty take BY DESIGN. Reconstructing the length from file size is possible future work; do not 'fix' the zero header into a lie instead.
nodes.norm_label: unfinalized take probes as zero frames

nodes.label: Audio Callback Performance Budget (2.67 ms at 48 kHz / 128 frames)
nodes.rationale: Targets to be measured in Phase 2 with a callback-duration histogram, not assumed, because CLAUDE.md §27 forbids optimising before measuring.
nodes.norm_label: audio callback performance budget (2.67 ms at 48 khz / 128 frames)

nodes.label: Reference Machine (Apple M5, 10 cores, 16 GB, macOS 26.2)
nodes.rationale: The 16 GB ceiling is treated as a real design constraint: it pushes the sampler toward disk streaming rather than full preload, and caps how many plugin instances a project can realistically hold.
nodes.norm_label: reference machine (apple m5, 10 cores, 16 gb, macos 26.2)

nodes.label: Performance Targets (audio, UI, project)
nodes.rationale: Headroom matters more than the average: a DAW that averages 40% of the callback budget but spikes to 110% glitches audibly, while one sitting flat at 60% does not. Startup must not scale with plugin collection size.

nodes.label: D-020 — A mixer strip is one node
nodes.rationale: One node rather than a chain of gain/pan/mute nodes, because a chain costs a buffer and an indirection per stage per block for arithmetic that fuses trivially.
nodes.community_name: D-020 — A mixer strip is one node
nodes.norm_label: d-020 — a mixer strip is one node

nodes.label: D-021 — Pan is constant power, centre is -3 dB
nodes.rationale: cos/sin of one angle with centre at 0.7071, because power rather than amplitude is what the ear tracks for a source moving across the stereo field.
nodes.community_name: D-020 — A mixer strip is one node
nodes.norm_label: d-021 — pan is constant power, centre is -3 db

nodes.label: Out-of-Process-Ready Plugin Host ABI
nodes.rationale: The host ABI is designed for out-of-process hosting from its first line even though in-process hosting ships first, because retrofitting isolation into an in-process design means rewriting the host and a crashing third-party plugin must never take down INCDAW or lose the user's project.

nodes.label: D-009 — Distribution: ad-hoc signed, un-notarized DMG
nodes.rationale: Ad-hoc signing (codesign -s -) is not cosmetic: arm64 binaries will not run unsigned. Notarization is deferred because it requires a paid developer account.
nodes.community_name: D-009 — Distribution: ad-hoc signed, un-notarized DMG
nodes.norm_label: d-009 — distribution: ad-hoc signed, un-notarized dmg

nodes.label: D-010 — Version control: git, initialised at Phase 0
nodes.rationale: git init on branch main with a macOS-aware .gitignore, because nothing else in the roadmap is safe without it.
nodes.community_name: D-010 — Version control: git, initialised at Phase 0
nodes.norm_label: d-010 — version control: git, initialised at phase 0

nodes.label: FL Studio Feature Parity Objective
nodes.rationale: FL Studio is a functional reference for capabilities and workflows only; proprietary source, algorithms, assets, presets and branding must not be copied.

nodes.label: Legal / IP Boundary
nodes.rationale: Equivalent functionality is allowed; proprietary implementation, reverse-engineered internals, copyrighted assets and trademarks are not.

nodes.label: ClapInstance
nodes.rationale: The concrete CLAP-backed instance: snapshots CLAP_EXT_PARAMS, implements engine::StateIO over CLAP_EXT_STATE, bridges CLAP_EXT_GUI for embedded Cocoa editors, and queries CLAP_EXT_LATENCY once while activated.

nodes.label: GraphCompileOptions::insertFactory
nodes.rationale: Keeps project/ free of any plugin header: the compiler asks the factory for an engine::Node per slot and the shell supplies one backed by the instance manager. A bypassed slot is not instantiated; an unbuildable slot becomes a pass-through plus a named compile warning, never silence and never a failed compile.

nodes.label: PluginNode
nodes.rationale: The render-graph node that owns a PluginInstance; its latencyFrames is just an ordinary node latency so the graph's existing compensation aligns parallel paths with no plugin-specific code in the engine.

nodes.label: plugins::PluginParameterInfo
nodes.rationale: Format-agnostic parameter description (plain min/max/default plus a stepped flag); non-automatable and malformed parameters are skipped as hostile input.

nodes.label: CLAP Format Support (first)
nodes.rationale: Chosen first (D-007) because it has the cleanest ABI, sample-accurate events and an explicit threading contract — the best format to build the host architecture on, and MIT licensed.

nodes.label: Plugin Latency Reporting and PDC Feed
nodes.rationale: Reported latency is capped at ten seconds because an absurd report must not make PDC build a giant delay line on every parallel path; clap_host_latency.changed lands on an atomic flag consumed by shell housekeeping which re-reads under the same cap and recompiles via the ordinary atomic swap. A manual per-instance offset exists because plugins reporting wrong latency is a known real-world problem.
nodes.norm_label: plugin latency reporting and pdc feed

nodes.label: PluginInstance (format-agnostic interface)
nodes.rationale: Wraps one loaded plugin so nothing above plugins/ ever sees a CLAP, AU or VST3 type — the engine knows only the interface, which is what keeps format additions from rippling upward.

nodes.label: PluginInstanceManager
nodes.rationale: Owns loaded libraries for the application's lifetime keyed by path, because graphs are rebuilt on every edit and retired asynchronously: a library owned by a graph would be unloaded while a node from it was still queued for destruction. Two instances share one opened binary and no binary closes while the app runs.

nodes.label: Release Notes 0.9.0
nodes.rationale: Marks the core complete (roadmap phases 0–19 plus release engineering). Known limits recorded deliberately: no AU/VST3 yet (CLAP first, D-007), no FLAC/MP3 (dependency approval pending), no MIDI clock out, in-process plugin crashes not survivable, and the UI is still the workshop version.

nodes.label: Phase 15 — Built-in DSP
nodes.rationale: Exit criterion: each effect passes a null test against its own reference implementation and all share one interface with no special-casing.

nodes.label: Phase 16 — MIDI Hardware and Controller Linking
nodes.rationale: Exit criterion: a control mapped by learn mode drives a mixer, instrument AND plugin parameter, and the mapping survives save/load — which is what forces mappings into the project format (v1.4).
nodes.norm_label: phase 16 — midi hardware and controller linking

nodes.label: Phase 17 — Rendering and Export
nodes.rationale: Exit criterion: offline render byte-identical to a realtime capture of the same project.

nodes.label: Phase 18 — Performance
nodes.rationale: Optimisation only where measurement justifies it (CLAUDE.md §27); exit criterion is that every optimisation has a documented before/after measurement. Instruments requires full Xcode, which is not installed — that becomes a dependency decision only if profiling proves necessary here.

nodes.label: Phase 19 — QA
nodes.rationale: Full regression suite, fuzzing of project loading and plugin scanning, plugin crash matrix, long-session stability and large-project stress; exit criterion is the whole suite green with no known crash-class defects open.

nodes.label: Performance Regression Baselines
nodes.rationale: Callback duration, UI frame time and project load time are measured in CI against recorded baselines, and a significant regression fails the build — performance is treated as a testable property, not a vibe.

nodes.label: Audio Engine
nodes.rationale: Critical subsystem; audio thread safety is a first-class architectural requirement.

nodes.label: Automation Subsystem
nodes.rationale: Automation must be a generic subsystem; never build it separately for every plugin or control.

nodes.label: Command Registry / Keyboard Shortcuts
nodes.rationale: Every action is a command; shortcuts must not be hardcoded inside UI components, keeping the system scripting-ready.

nodes.label: Content / Sound Library
nodes.rationale: Do not bundle copyrighted commercial content; use original, demo or public-domain assets.

nodes.label: Controller Linking
nodes.rationale: A single generic parameter mapping system rather than per-surface mappings.

nodes.label: Clip / Project Data Model
nodes.rationale: Distinct entity types must not be collapsed into one generic object.

nodes.label: Built-in Effect Framework
nodes.rationale: Effects must share a common DSP/plugin interface.

nodes.label: INCDAW
nodes.rationale: Must not be treated as a toy DAW, demo, prototype, mockup or UI-only app; architected so features can be added without rewriting the audio engine.

nodes.label: Built-in Instrument Framework
nodes.rationale: Build the instrument API first rather than attempting all instruments at once.

nodes.label: Mixer
nodes.rationale: Routing must support arbitrary graph-like signal flow where safe; avoid hardcoded linear signal chains.

nodes.label: Offline Render Engine
nodes.rationale: Realtime and offline processing must use compatible DSP paths where possible.

nodes.label: Pattern System
nodes.rationale: Patterns must be reusable, independently editable, and placeable into the arrangement.

nodes.label: Piano Roll
nodes.rationale: First-class editing environment; performance must remain usable with very large note counts.

nodes.label: Playlist / Arrangement
nodes.rationale: Architecture must not assume a simplistic 1:1 track-to-mixer relationship; the routing model must stay flexible.

nodes.label: Plugin Host
nodes.rationale: Third-party plugins are never assumed safe; the host must be resilient to plugin crashes and invalid behavior.

nodes.label: Time Stretching / Pitch Architecture
nodes.rationale: Must be pluggable with realtime preview and offline high-quality modes; a low-quality placeholder must not be considered complete.

nodes.label: UI Architecture
nodes.rationale: Modular dockable workspaces with INCDAW's own visual identity; do not copy FL Studio's exact visual design.

nodes.label: Undo / Redo
nodes.rationale: Prefer a command-based architecture; avoid ad-hoc undo implementations.

nodes.label: Engineering Rules
nodes.rationale: No God classes, no circular dependencies, no UI/DSP coupling, no serialization inside UI, no routing logic in visual components.

nodes.label: MPE Readiness
nodes.rationale: Architecture should be prepared for future MPE support rather than retrofitted later.

nodes.label: Performance Strategy
nodes.rationale: Performance is a feature; profile before optimizing and never optimize based on assumptions.

nodes.label: Versioned Project Format
nodes.rationale: The project format must be versioned from day one (INCDAW_PROJECT_VERSION) so future migrations remain possible; never create an unversioned format.

nodes.label: Realtime Audio Thread Safety
nodes.rationale: The realtime audio thread must never allocate unnecessarily, block on I/O, do network operations, wait for UI, or take locks that risk priority inversion.

nodes.label: engine/audio/AudioStream + DiskStreamer (D-025)
nodes.rationale: Two segments leapfrog ahead of the play position, each under its own seqlock; the realtime read is wait-free and what the window cannot serve is zero-filled and COUNTED, never waited for. Seeks are just a requested position the next service pass moves the window to.

nodes.label: EBU R128 loudness (incdaw.loudness)
nodes.rationale: BS.1770-4 K-weighting designed per sample rate; momentary, short-term and gated integrated loudness via a constant-memory histogram, calibrated to the -3.01 LUFS reference.

nodes.label: engine::dsp::MetronomeNode
nodes.rationale: Existed since Phase 3 and was in no graph. Now compiled in when the toggle is on and mixed into the master so it can never reach a render or a stem; it takes a tempo map rather than the transport and reads transport state from the block like every other node.

nodes.label: engine/dsp/MixerStripNode
nodes.rationale: Summing, polarity, constant-power pan, fader, mute and metering in ONE pass (D-020, D-021), later joined by stereo separation with a click-free ramp and a unity tap spliced ahead of the fader for true pre-fader sends.

nodes.label: MoveInsertCommand (insert reordering)
nodes.rationale: Chain order is signal order, no longer only add order.

nodes.label: ProcessContext::playing (transport state per block)
nodes.rationale: A stopped transport must keep rendering (synth releases, delay tails, input monitoring), so the block carries the SAME position every time. Timeline readers render nothing while parked; sequenced notes end ONCE on the first stopped block; automation keeps evaluating; offline rendering is untouched because the flag defaults to true.

nodes.label: project::compileProjectGraph
nodes.rationale: The Project -> render graph seam with an injectable InstrumentFactory and insertFactory returning engine::Node, so project/ places hosted plugins in the graph without including a plugin header (D-028). Separate input and output indices per mixer node put signal into the head of the insert chain and out at the strip.

nodes.label: engine::SampleCache (D-032)
nodes.rationale: Decoded audio cached by (path, size, mtime) and shared immutably across graph rebuilds, owned by the app and passed via GraphCompileOptions, so neither sampler zones nor preloaded clips re-decode per rebuild.

nodes.label: engine/instrument/Sampler
nodes.rationale: Zones in, sample-accurate voices out; key/velocity LAYERING falls out of several zones matching one note. Repitches by rate through linear interpolation because a sampler is not time stretching (§16). setZones is build-time only, following the structural-edit contract: a zone edit is a graph rebuild.

nodes.label: engine::SamplerZoneStream (head + pool)
nodes.rationale: The first ~1.4 s stay decoded in RAM so a note starts instantly; past the head a voice reads from one of 4 pooled AudioStreams steered to the hand-over point at note-on. Slots are claimed wait-free; more held notes than slots degrade to head-only voices rather than blocking or allocating. Looped and reversed zones preload whole because a loop must be resident to be seamless.

nodes.label: SetTempoCommand
nodes.rationale: Merges, so a tempo drag is one undo entry; the project is the source of truth, the transport takes the same map, and the graph rebuilds.

nodes.label: Slicer (detectOnsets + SliceAssetCommand)
nodes.rationale: One undo lands a sampler channel (a zone per slice, chromatic keys) AND the pattern replaying the loop's timing.

nodes.label: The hum at idle (block-rate retrigger defect)
nodes.rationale: The default project's first note sits on tick 0 and the playhead parks there, so InstrumentNode re-collected the note ~94 times a second (hard-killing the voice in between via the discontinuity check) and AudioClipNode replayed the few hundred frames under the playhead forever. What the ear heard was a hum at the block rate.
nodes.norm_label: the hum at idle (block-rate retrigger defect)

nodes.label: Sidechain routing (detector-only key inputs)
nodes.rationale: Sidechain edges compile into detector-only key inputs on the destination's compressor inserts, PDC-aligned and never summed into audio.

nodes.label: Three-worktree consolidation (2026-08-20)
nodes.rationale: Three parallel branches (UI build-out increments 1-10, the FL2026 feature wave, the drawn design language) had never merged back; they were merged in dependency order with conflicts resolved SEMANTICALLY, not textually. A fourth branch was dropped because its single commit was superseded.

nodes.label: Compiled graph owns its own tempo map
nodes.rationale: Nodes converting ticks to frames hold a pointer to the graph's copy for as long as they render, so a map shared with the transport cannot be rewritten while the audio thread is inside it. A tempo edit is a rebuild: the new graph carries the new map, the old one keeps the map it was compiled against until retired. Before this, a vector reallocation under a binary search was a crash waiting for a tempo drag.
nodes.norm_label: compiled graph owns its own tempo map

nodes.label: Format 1.5/1.6 renumbering on merge
nodes.rationale: Both merged lines had independently claimed format 1.5. Instrument parameters kept 1.5; markers, regions and stereo width became 1.6 with the additive migration and tests/fixtures/v1.6/ rebased to match. D-034 likewise stayed with instrument parameters and the design language became D-035.

nodes.label: Shared-device block size hazard
nodes.rationale: A device shared with another process delivers whatever block size CoreAudio is servicing, not what the property query reports. GraphCompileOptions.maxBlockSize must come from AudioEngine::maxServiceableBlockSize; a graph compiled smaller renders the first part of the block and leaves the rest silent, which the ear hears as a buzz (AirPods report 15..960 against a 256-frame graph). CoreAudioDevice also records and restores the shared device's buffer size on close, or quitting INCDAW leaves every other application's audio broken.

nodes.label: app::AppSettings
nodes.rationale: Settings are not project data (D-036) — device, rate, block size and workspace state persist beside the app, never inside a .incdaw package.

nodes.label: engine::AuditionPlayer (browser preview)
nodes.rationale: Mixed by the engine AFTER the project graph so it sounds with the transport stopped and never costs a graph rebuild. The audio thread reads a raw pointer; the decoded buffer is released only once the block counter has passed the swap — the same grace a retired graph gets.

nodes.label: app::Browser + INCDAWBrowserView
nodes.rationale: Roots, folders-first listings, recursive search capped at 500 results and 8 levels, favourites and recents — all persisted beside the plugin catalogue, NEVER inside a project. Project packages and plugin bundles are named as themselves and never descended into.

nodes.label: Piano Roll chord toolkit (app::music)
nodes.rationale: Chord detection with inversion naming, chord stamping with bottom-up/top-down voicings, movement-minimising voice-leading and diatonic progression nudge — the FL Chord Panel capability reimplemented independently.

nodes.label: Command Search palette (Cmd+K)
nodes.rationale: The palette WALKS THE MENU BAR so an entry can never drift from the menu it mirrors, shortcut included, and lists the registry's actions plus live undo/redo beside them.

nodes.label: app::registerStandardActions
nodes.rationale: Gives Add Channel/Pattern/Track ids that the palette, a shortcut, a controller mapping or a future script can all reach (CLAUDE.md §26). Lives in app/, not in the shell, so it is testable — the registry's table was empty in the running application before this.

nodes.label: ui/macos/Theme — the drawn design language
nodes.rationale: One visual vocabulary (Ink palette roles, metrics, type, and primitives: panel, well, step pad, region, transport button, knob, slider, fader, meter, toggle, LCD, tab, playhead) instead of per-pane greys. FL Studio's density inside GarageBand's calm, drawn from primitives — nothing copied from either product. No view in the shell declares a colour of its own.

nodes.label: incdaw_app layer library
nodes.rationale: Command registry, undo and headless view models live here rather than in the shell so that every decision the UI makes is testable without AppKit.

nodes.label: Audio and MIDI Settings window (Cmd+,)
nodes.rationale: Applying reopens the device and MIDI client in place; the playhead is preserved in TICKS so a sample-rate change cannot move it, and the status line reports what the device GRANTED rather than what was asked for. A device that refuses to open falls back to the system default rather than leaving the app silent.

nodes.label: MIDI hardware link (MidiDevice -> MidiInput)
nodes.rationale: The last missing link in a chain complete and tested since Phase 5: a keyboard reached CoreMIDI and stopped there, which made live playing and MIDI learn dead ends in the running application. An empty source list means every source.

nodes.label: Workspace persistence (frame, pane, mode)
nodes.rationale: A restored frame that no longer lands on an attached screen is centred rather than restored off the edge.

nodes.label: One undo caller path (D-037)
nodes.rationale: Undo/redo route through ONE shell path that resyncs every pane, which also fixes the Piano Roll holding selection indices into notes an undo taken in another pane had already removed. Cmd+Z is handed back to the field editor while a text field has focus.

nodes.label: Single source of truth for the version
nodes.rationale: PROJECT_VERSION is written to ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/VERSION and consumed by tools/make-dmg.sh and app/Version, so the binary, the bundle and the DMG name cannot disagree.
nodes.norm_label: single source of truth for the version

nodes.label: Deliberately dark-only colour scheme
nodes.rationale: The Ink indirection allows a second palette table, but the scheme is dark-only for now because CLAUDE.md §25 asks for a dark professional interface.
